questions.question: Driving has risks. It is smart to keep improving your driving and observation skills.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Driving becomes unsafe if you think you have nothing left to learn. Always work to improve your driving and observation skills for your safety and the safety of others.

questions.question: When railroad crossing gates are down and red lights are flashing, you should:

options.text: Stop and only proceed when the gates are raised and lights stop flashing.
Drive around the gates after stopping.
Drive side by side with the train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only proceed when the gates are raised and lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when you see flashing warning lights and lowered gates at a railroad crossing. Wait until the gate rises and the lights stop flashing before moving. Never drive around lowered gates. It is illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them so they won't cross against red lights again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Let pedestrians and other vehicles cross safely, even when you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn and keep your speed.
Speed up to leave the area quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. Slow down and be ready to stop if a pedestrian crosses.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The railroad crossing is controlled. Drive at your normal speed.
Look and listen. Be ready to stop if needed.
Stop at the tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look and listen. Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for trains to pass before crossing.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver:

options.text: Relax and focus on driving.
Drive above the posted speed limit.
Tailgate the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: Stay calm and focus on driving. Don't take other drivers' actions personally. Plan extra time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding and driving too fast for the conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and staying focused.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding and driving too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving above the speed limit or too fast for road conditions causes crashes. Always drive at legal speeds and match the flow of traffic.

questions.question: Changing lanes is best done:

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Slowly and carefully.

questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and carefully. Only change lanes when you must. Each lane change increases crash risk.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger tells you to stop.
There is a stop sign.
Flashing red lights and gates are working.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop when a flagger or stop sign tells you to. Also stop when flashing red lights and gates are present and working.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle. You should:

options.text: Not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Hide that you don't know how to use this vehicle.
Ignore any problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where all the controls are and how to use them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where all the controls are and how to use them.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, spend time learning the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: What should you do if you meet an aggressive driver?

options.text: Challenge them.
Get out of their way.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: The safest choice is to get out of their way. Do not compete with other drivers. Avoid road rage by staying calm and letting aggressive drivers pass.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no traffic coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop at a red light. This is the law. Running a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if there is no sign that says you cannot.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver cuts you off?

options.text: Pull next to them and yell.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams.
Cut them off to get back at them.

questions.explanation: Do not take it personally. Let it go and keep driving safely. This helps you avoid road rage and dangerous situations.

questions.question: What do flashing amber lights on a school bus mean?

options.text: The driver is changing gears.
The bus will soon stop to pick up or drop off children.
The driver is about to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bus will soon stop to pick up or drop off children.
questions.explanation: Flashing amber lights warn you that the bus will stop soon. Slow down to 20 mph or less and be ready to stop. Do not pass the bus when the amber lights are flashing.

questions.question: What is a result of driving too fast?

options.text: You save time getting to your destination.
You can avoid obstacles more easily.
It increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and leads to poor driving choices. It greatly increases the danger of accidents.

questions.question: What must you do if a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone?

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says something different.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic laws as if the construction zone was not there.

questions.explanation: Always follow a flagger's directions in a construction zone. Ignoring them is illegal and puts workers at risk.

questions.question: What can happen if you mix prescription drugs and alcohol?

options.text: Nothing will happen.
You will be more alert.
You may not be safe to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be safe to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can reduce your ability to drive. Mixing them with alcohol makes this much worse and is very dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Parking reserved for people with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking reserved for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces for people with disability license plates, disabled veteran plates, or disability placards.

questions.question: What should you do if you get drowsy while driving?

options.text: Fight the drowsiness.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.explanation: Stop at a rest area to nap, stretch, or let someone else drive. Caffeine pills and energy drinks do not replace real rest and can make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the turn signals.
You may not see the brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too close and the car ahead stops or slows down, you may crash into it. Keep a safe distance so you have time to stop.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are usually not important.
They are only found in construction zones.
They give information to drivers.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers. They show drivers where to position their vehicles, indicate safe passing areas, and warn about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. When must you stop?

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if flashing red lights are on, a gate is down, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is visible or close. If you are unsure, stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the steering wheel and ask passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your vehicle unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance card.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When you see railroad crossing signs, slow down, look for trains, and be ready to stop. If red warning lights flash or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not drive around the gate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
The road is slippery when wet.
The road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions just ahead. This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a detour ahead.
You must stop for flaggers.
The road is closed to traffic.
Roadwork is ahead.

questions.explanation: Construction signs are orange. They warn drivers about unusual or dangerous conditions in work areas. This sign tells drivers that roadwork is coming and they should slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal before moving your vehicle left or right to alert other drivers. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can be dangerous to infants and small children, even in low-speed crashes.
Make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce injuries and deaths in crashes. Children age 12 and under should ride properly restrained in a rear seat. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front of a vehicle with a front passenger airbag.

questions.question: When a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street, what must you do?

options.text: Always yield the right-of-way.
Tell them where to cross the street.
Only yield the right-of-way at a corner.

questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians may use a guide dog or carry a white cane. Always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians using a guide dog or carrying a white cane.

questions.question: When approaching a parked police car, tow truck, or utility vehicle with flashing lights, what should you do?

options.text: Stop abruptly.
Continue as usual.
Change lanes and slow to a safe speed as you pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and slow to a safe speed as you pass.
questions.explanation: When approaching a parked police car, tow truck, or other vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it space if possible. If you cannot change lanes, slow down and pass safely.
